current.text: In an auction mock, Josh valued Wagner at 11 to 15 USD. He went for 15 USD, which Josh called about right.
In snake drafts he goes around picks 54 to 60. Experts took him in round 6 and called picks 47 and 49 a bit early.
His draft price has fallen because of his injury history.
Last season was hurt by an ankle injury and lower minutes.
His upside this season is about top 40, not top 30.
He is a projected starter next to Suggs, Bane, Banchero and Carter. That group was very good when it played together.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, so roles may change.
Phil projects Orlando for 47 or 48 wins and the 6th seed.

durable.text: He has no single standout category but is good across the board. FT%, points and assists for a forward are his best areas.
He is probably better in category leagues than in points leagues.
He has had two seasons badly shortened by injury, each after a poor shooting season. In 2025-26 he missed about 47 to 51 games with a high ankle sprain from a contact injury.
Before those two seasons he was usually reliable and played through ankle rolls.
Phil sees the injuries of the last two years as random, not chronic.

note: The sites disagree on his price: Yahoo values him at 21 USD (11.4 USD average cost) and ESPN at 7 USD. He went for 26 USD in our league last season, and Josh's 11 to 15 USD range fits his current rank of about 50 to 65. He has no weak category, so he fits any build. His best areas are FT% (z +1.3), points and assists for a forward, which makes him a solid mid-tier piece in the 15 USD range rather than a reach at last season's price. Early in the season, check how his ankle holds up and whether new coach Sweeney gives him his old 33 to 34 minutes, not the 30.0 he played last season.
